candidates.justification: v1.1 names a cluster with the gap rule and then merges clusters whose dependence buffers overlap. The buffer exists so origins near an event are not treated as independent evidence. Overlap of two buffers is not a reason to call the clusters one spell. Dropping the window merge keeps the buffer available for a later deletion rule and lets the gap rule name the episode. The reason is the two-step structure of the frozen rule. It is not a skill result, and it is not the floor column.
candidates.title: Frozen gap, no window merge

candidates.justification: v1.1 lets the label horizon set the gap, so a longer outcome window is also a longer chain. The frozen rule already contains a dependence scale that is not the label horizon: the 21-session pre-window. A quiet-reset at 21, on each horizon's own event dates, with no window merge, uses that scale at every horizon. The union's event-date occupancy is why a gap as short as the label horizon chains sessions. A v1.2 preregistration has to disclose that this density was seen. 21 is taken from the pre-window constant. It is not taken from the rows that clear the floor.
candidates.title: Quiet-reset at Q=21, no window merge, same Q at every horizon

candidates.justification: The panel event date is any session on which at least one name has Y=1. That union is what fills the date axis. A spell that is supposed to be shared needs a second name on the session. m=2 is that minimum confirmation. It is a property of a common-move question. This memo has no episode count for it: the artifacts do not store per-date breadth. A preregistration that wants a breadth rule has to keep those counts and must not choose m by which value clears the floor on this sample.
candidates.title: Breadth threshold m=2, after per-date counts are retained

disclosure: this rule was chosen after observing v1.1 event-date density (not skill)
floor_warning: Choosing a rule because it meets the 10-episode / 10-month floor on this consumed sample is p-hacking the power floor.

not_computable.name: Breadth threshold
not_computable.needs: The per-session count of names with Y=1 on the comparison-set date axis, or the per-name event dates that would produce it. The committed union records only that the count was at least one. The ticker-event total is a sum across sessions, not a per-date histogram.
not_computable.rule: A session is a panel event date only when at least m names have Y=1 on that session. A predeclared gap and window then run on the dates that survive.

not_computable.name: Per-ticker episodes with a common-shock correction
not_computable.needs: Per-name event dates or per-name episode windows. The artifact stores the per-name episode count only, so overlap across names cannot be recovered.
not_computable.rule: Count episodes on each name, then treat episodes that overlap in time as one common shock. Honest-N is the number of common shocks, not the sum of the per-name counts.

not_computable.name: Sector-stratified episodes
not_computable.needs: Per-name event dates. The sector labels of these ETFs can be named without data. The dates cannot. A group union cannot be rebuilt from the panel-wide union or from per-name counts.
not_computable.rule: Form the union of event dates inside a predeclared grouping of names, then run the episode rule inside each group.
